evidence_requests.question: Do the current candidate sets each have a coherent and interpretable biological identity in the discovery modalities?
Are the current membership, boundaries, and granularity defensible across modalities, or is there reproducible internal subdivision or insufficient separation between sets?
Could measured technical, acquisition, or site-related factors plausibly explain the signals defining these candidate sets?
What is the relationship between the current partition and assessed stage/grade labels?

actions.reason: C0001 has coherent WXS identity evidence (PBRM1/VHL enrichment), no technical confounder association, and cross-modal boundary separation that is positive against all other sets with WXS driving a clean separation; the current membership and granularity are defensible for downstream validation.

C0002 shows coherent RNA metabolic-downregulation and WXS (FLG/PTEN, VHL-depleted) identity signals, no technical confounder association, and positive fused boundary separation against all other sets, supporting retention of the current membership.

C0003 has strong coherent RNA (fatty acid metabolism up, inflammatory/EMT down) and WXS (MUC16/DST) identity evidence, no technical confounder association, and positive fused boundary separation against all other sets, supporting the current representation.

C0004 has very strong WXS identity evidence (BAP1 enrichment, PBRM1 depletion) with a coherent immune-up RNA trend, no technical confounder association, and positive fused boundary separation against all other sets, supporting retention.

C0005 has strong WXS identity evidence (ATM/PBRM1/KDM5C enrichment), no technical confounder association, and positive fused boundary separation against all other sets, supporting the current membership despite small set size.

C0006 has strong WXS identity evidence (VHL and PBRM1 depletion) with a coherent metabolic-down RNA trend, no technical confounder association, and positive fused boundary separation against all other sets, supporting retention.

C0007 has strong WXS identity evidence (universal VHL mutation, PBRM1 depletion), no technical confounder association, and positive fused boundary separation against all other sets, supporting the current representation.

C0008 has only weak identity evidence (LYST enrichment based on 3/4 patients, nonsignificant RNA/CNV) and limited cross-modal coherence with internal structure not fully estimable at n=4; no technical confounder association and positive fused boundary separation against all other sets, so it is retained as a discovery-stage candidate with explicit uncertainty for downstream validation.
